mods.name: DrawLess
mods.description: Client-side rendering optimizations for Item Display scenes and particles.

releases.notes:
**DrawLess 1.2.0 — Player armor on the GPU.**

DrawLess 1.2.0 starts optimizing player rendering. Player armor now stays on the
GPU instead of being rebuilt every frame, and new player profiling shows where
player rendering spends its CPU time.

**Players**

- New **Players** settings page with **GPU armor geometry**, **ON by default**.
  A configuration that saved this option as OFF keeps it OFF.
- Armor model parts keep their geometry on the GPU; each frame sends only part
  poses, lighting and tint. Animation and the normal model traversal stay live.
- Base armor textures share one texture atlas, so armor layers, trims and
  enchantment glint draw in a few calls instead of one per armor texture.
- Base layers, overlays, trims and glint of one armor piece always use the same
  path, so glint and trims line up exactly. Glowing players, animated textures,
  non-vanilla armor models and textures that cannot be packed use ordinary rendering.
- Armor in the inventory and other menu previews always uses ordinary rendering.

**Measurements**

- Added `/drawless profile players <label> [control|stages|deep]`: a sampled
  CPU profile of player extraction, layers, model preparation, name tags and
  drawing, saved as a readable report and JSON.
- Added the `player_armor` target for automated comparisons, for example
  `/drawless benchmark 3 armor player_armor`.

**Compatibility**

GPU armor is disabled with Iris and with resource packs that replace the entity
or glint shaders; existing ImmediatelyFast and Iris exclusions remain in place.
Tested with Sodium 0.9.2 and ImmediatelyFast 1.16.5. These safeguards do not
imply validation with every combination of rendering or model mods.

**Performance and limitations**

In alternating player profiles on a live server scene with about 28 visible
players, armor rendering CPU dropped by about 1.3 ms per frame, with no visual
differences noticed. FPS in that scene varied too much with the player count
for a headline FPS claim, and GPU time was not measured. Existing public
benchmarks keep their original build labels and conditions.

Glint is drawn after solid armor and before translucent objects. Local native
frame comparisons (standalone and with Sodium + ImmediatelyFast, with and without
improved transparency) matched vanilla behind water, stained glass, translucent
item displays and slimes; behind a text display with a semi-transparent
background, glint stays slightly more visible than in vanilla (up to 9/255 per
channel). A rejected earlier armor approach is recorded in
[the decision log](https://github.com/WilyFoxM/DrawLess/blob/main/docs/REJECTED_OPTIMIZATIONS.md).

**Requirements**

Minecraft **26.2**, Fabric Loader **0.19.3+**, Fabric API **0.161.0+26.2** and
Java **25**. Sodium is optional; no server-side installation is needed.

Thanks to **fzzyhmstrs and the Particle Core contributors**, alongside
**RK_01 / RaphiMC**, the **ImmediatelyFast contributors**, **LlamaLad7** and the
**MixinExtras contributors**. [Attributions and reference links](https://github.com/WilyFoxM/DrawLess#attributions).

mods.description: Client-side rendering optimizations for Item Display scenes and particles.

releases.notes:
**DrawLess 1.1.0 — Less repeated work. Better measurements.**

DrawLess 1.1.0 improves particle lighting and collision reuse, and adds automated
comparisons to help measure what the optimizations actually save in your scene.

**Particles**

- Particle light and empty-collision caches are now **ON by default for new settings**.
  Existing saved ON/OFF choices are preserved. Both switches remain available under
  **F8 → Particles**.
- Reuse base particle lighting across rendering passes within a valid client tick,
  with invalidation when blocks, chunks or published lighting change.
- Reuse immutable block positions and a bounded table of chunk references and block
  states, avoiding repeated world reads across overlapping collision checks.
- Skip collision collection for empty air sections and non-air shapes verified as
  empty for the current collision context. Unsupported cases use ordinary collision
  handling, without reducing particle counts or pausing their simulation.
- Release retained world data on disconnect, world changes and resource reloads.

**Measurements**

- Added automated **OFF → ON → OFF** comparisons, with one or three bracketed ON
  runs. Compare the whole mod, particle caches together, individual particle caches,
  text reuse or feature batching.
- Save per-phase reports, a readable summary and JSON measurements; restore the
  original settings afterwards. Detect camera/settings changes and focus loss,
  and temporarily prevent Minecraft's AFK frame cap from contaminating a series.
- Expanded particle CPU and cache diagnostics, including shared-state hits,
  physical proof-state reads and context maintenance. These CPU scopes do not
  measure GPU execution or all shared upload costs.

For example, `/drawless benchmark 3 smoke particles` compares both particle caches
with three bracketed ON runs. Use `/drawless benchmark cancel` to stop a series.

**Compatibility**

Overlapping particle caches are disabled when Particle Core or AsyncParticles is
present. With Iris or recognized dynamic-light integrations, light reuse stays
within the current rendering pass. Existing ImmediatelyFast and Iris rendering
exclusions remain in place. These safeguards do not imply validation with every
combination of optimization mods.

**Performance and limitations**

Local checks and a live-scene comparison showed lower particle CPU costs, with no
visible differences reported in that field session. Scene variation prevents a
new headline FPS claim or a release-to-release improvement percentage. Existing
public benchmarks keep their original build labels and conditions.

EXPANDED batching can still change overlapping layers; select LIMITED or OFF if
needed. Rejected particle experiments and their costs are recorded in
[the decision log](https://github.com/WilyFoxM/DrawLess/blob/main/docs/REJECTED_OPTIMIZATIONS.md).

**Requirements**

Minecraft **26.2**, Fabric Loader **0.19.3+**, Fabric API **0.161.0+26.2** and
Java **25**. Sodium is optional; no server-side installation is needed.

Thanks to **fzzyhmstrs and the Particle Core contributors**, alongside
**RK_01 / RaphiMC**, the **ImmediatelyFast contributors**, **LlamaLad7** and the
**MixinExtras contributors**. [Attributions and reference links](https://github.com/WilyFoxM/DrawLess#attributions).

releases.notes:
DrawLess 1.0.0 — Less work. Clearer controls.
DrawLess 1.0.0 brings a redesigned settings experience and improved rendering compatibility, making its existing optimizations easier to configure and use alongside other mods.
What’s new
- A new navy-and-orange settings menu, organized into Rendering, Particles, Advanced and Diagnostics.
- Global search and explanatory tooltips.
- Clear ON/OFF switches, reversible mode selectors and draggable numbers with live Shift precision.
- Full keyboard navigation, including Tab, arrow keys, Ctrl+F and Page Up/Down.
- English and Russian translations that follow the Minecraft language setting.
- Automatic saving, reset confirmation and a retry action if settings cannot be saved.
- A compact 32×32 mod icon, reducing the release JAR from 1.39 MiB to 220.2 KiB — 84.6% smaller.
Controls
Open settings with F8, rebindable under Options → Controls → Key Binds → DrawLess. The old /drawless settings and bare /drawless menu shortcuts have been removed; diagnostic subcommands remain available. Existing saved settings are preserved.
Compatibility
Reworked 18 rendering call-site hooks to use composable operation wrappers, reducing conflicts when other mods modify the same calls. Ordinary fallbacks preserve the surrounding hook chain. ImmediatelyFast and Iris exclusions remain in place; compatibility with every renderer is not guaranteed.
Performance
This release focuses on usability and compatibility. No new FPS improvement over 0.2.0 is claimed. Existing benchmarks retain their original build labels and conditions.
[Full results, raw measurements and limitations](https://github.com/WilyFoxM/DrawLess/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md).
Known limitations
EXPANDED batching remains the default and can change overlapping layers. If text backgrounds or other layers look incorrect, select LIMITED or OFF under Rendering → Feature batching. Optional text reuse and particle caches remain experimental and OFF by default.
Requirements
Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API 0.161.0+26.2 and Java 25. Sodium is optional; no server-side installation is needed.
Thanks to RK_01 / RaphiMC, the ImmediatelyFast contributors, LlamaLad7 and the MixinExtras contributors. [Attributions and reference links](https://github.com/WilyFoxM/DrawLess#attributions).

releases.notes:
**DrawLess 0.2.0 — Expanded feature batching**
DrawLess 0.2.0 broadens feature batching to combine compatible material draws across more rendering groups, reducing separate draw submissions where the scene allows it.

**What’s new**
- EXPANDED batching enabled by default for new configurations and after resetting settings.
- Three batching modes: OFF, LIMITED and EXPANDED. Existing saved choices are preserved.
- Optional text and name-tag buffer reuse, with pass-local ownership and active-buffer validation. OFF by default.
- Improved diagnostics: requested/effective modes, material reuse counters and CPU search/submission scopes.
- Overlapping text/batching hooks are excluded when ImmediatelyFast is installed. Iris also disables feature batching.
- Source distributions now include the project’s MIT license.

**Performance**
A separate 0.2.0-dev.4 benchmark recorded +34.53% mean paired FPS change in one animated Item Display scene: 241.88 FPS bracketed OFF baseline versus 325.39 FPS ON.
That test used Sodium, EXPANDED batching and optional text reuse, with particle caches OFF. It is not a measured improvement over 0.1.0 or a benchmark of final 0.2.0 defaults. OFF controls varied by 12.03%, and the Display population changed late in the series.
[Full results, all seven phases, raw measurements and limitations](https://github.com/WilyFoxM/DrawLess/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md).

**Known limitations**
EXPANDED can change the appearance of overlapping transparent or opaque layers because it permits broader draw reordering. If text backgrounds or other layers look incorrect, select LIMITED or OFF under /drawless settings → Advanced.
FPS gains depend on the scene and rendering bottleneck; no general improvement in frame-time stability is claimed.

**Requirements**
Minecraft 26.2, Fabric Loader 0.19.3+, Fabric API and Java 25. Sodium is optional.
Thanks to RK_01 / RaphiMC and the ImmediatelyFast contributors for the reference approaches. Detailed attribution and pinned source links are available in the README.
